trust_decision.summary: In the global branch of String.prototype.match the addon loops on re2->regexp.Match and advances with byteIndex = match.data() - str.data + match.size(); a zero-width match has size()==0, so byteIndex never moves, the loop re-matches at the same offset forever and pushes every result into a std::vector<StringPiece> until native memory is exhausted (CWE-835 / DoS).

landing_point.why: The report names global String.prototype.match; this is the only global match loop in the pinned tree, and line 48 is the only place in it where a zero-width match fails to advance the cursor.

fix_sites.entry_point: String.prototype.match(re2) / re2[Symbol.match](str) / re2.match(str) (prototype method registered at lib/addon.cc:89, aliased to Symbol.match at re2.js:17-22)
fix_sites.module_kind: C++ addon method (Nan), global match branch - this is the flaw in GHSA-6HXR-MR5R-9836

fix_sites.entry_point: every lastIndex-taking method (exec/match/replace/split/test) through the cached subject string in prepareArgument
fix_sites.module_kind: C++ addon string cache - this hunk belongs to the bundled GHSA-ff84-5f28-78qj (lastIndex OOB read), not to this DoS

fix_sites.entry_point: every lastIndex-taking method via StrVal::setIndex -> getUtf16PositionByCounter
fix_sites.module_kind: C++ addon index mapping (StrVal) - bundled GHSA-ff84-5f28-78qj
inline header helper, lower-level API - bundled GHSA-ff84-5f28-78qj

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site for this flaw: the only other global-iteration routes into the same sink (lib/replace.cc:259-273 and lib/replace.cc:446-460, lib/split.cc:44-55, re2.js:24-38 matchAll) already advance on a zero-width match, so a solver has nothing to argue out of scope - and the host therefore offers no scope lever either.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Zero-width matches must still be returned and must not suppress the result: native parity requires 'x'.match(/a*/g) -> ['',''], ''.match(/a*/g) -> [''] and null only when there is no match at all (groups.empty() branch). An over-broad fix that breaks out of the loop on an empty match, skips/dedupes empty matches, or advances by one byte corrupts exactly these results.

O6_input_shapes: non-ASCII / multi-byte UTF-8 subject (advance must be one code point: 'hello-accent' cases in fix.diff:146-148)
zero-width match at start, middle and end of the subject ('a*', 'b?', 'x{0,3}', '(a)|', '(?:)', 'c*d*')

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a JS-level global iteration (the Symbol.matchAll generator) that advances lastIndex itself when result[0] === ''
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the maintainer already wrote this exact loop in JavaScript as the sibling of the C++ global match; a new JS entry point over the same iteration (Buffer subjects, or code-point-aware advance under 'u') would naturally copy the same ++re.lastIndex line.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second C++ global scan whose empty-match branch reads str.data[byteIndex] instead of the match offset
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: split.cc already duplicates the zero-width advance that replace.cc has; a new scanner (for example a C++ matchAll or an RE2.Set iterator) would be written from this template.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a separate global loop serving Buffer subjects or the 'd' (hasIndices) flag
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: match.cc already forks string/buffer result formatting after the loop (lib/match.cc:81-146), so a maintainer extending the global branch with indices could add a second iteration rather than share one.

O9_family: CWE-835 infinite loop / unbounded native allocation in regex global iteration (resource exhaustion)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: `if (!match.size()) break;` (or skipping/deduping empty matches) - stops the hang but returns null instead of ['',''] for 'x'.match(/a*/g); or `byteIndex = offset + 1`, which is correct on ASCII but makes 'hello-accent'.match(new RE2('x*','g')) return one empty match per byte instead of per code point.

out_of_scope_notes: The same commit also fixes a distinct advisory, GHSA-ff84-5f28-78qj (out-of-range lastIndex on a non-ASCII subject -> read past the buffer), at lib/addon.cc:200-209, lib/addon.cc:263 and lib/wrapped_re2.h:264-275; that is a different weakness from this CWE-835 DoS and is not screened here.
